It outlines capital augmentation options (subordinated debt, preference shares, perpetual instruments, equity) and strategic capital planning for foreign subsidiaries. Quantitatively, it details capital requirements for credit risk (standardized approach, securitization), market risk (standardized duration approach for interest rate, forex, equity), operational risk (Basic Indicator Approach), and provides CET1, Tier 1, and Total Capital Ratios for the consolidated group and significant bank subsidiaries.

structure.title: DF-3: CREDIT RISK: GENERAL DISCLOSURES

Qualitatively, it defines non-performing assets (NPAs), out-of-order and overdue statuses, stressed asset resolution including SMA categories, and discusses the Bank's Credit Risk Management Policy, covering identification, assessment, measurement, monitoring, and control of credit risk. It also details credit risk assessment models, industry research, exposure limits, stress testing, loan policy, credit audit, and risk mitigation. Quantitatively, it provides gross credit risk exposures, geographic distribution (domestic/overseas), industry-wise distribution of fund-based and non-fund-based exposures, residual contractual maturity breakdown of assets, amounts of gross and net NPAs, NPA ratios, movement of NPAs and provisions, non-performing investments, provisions for depreciation on investments, and industry/geographic distribution of NPAs with specific and general provisions. Tables include industry type distribution and maturity breakdown.

structure.title: DF–7: MARKET RISK IN TRADING BOOK

structure.title: DF–9: INTEREST RATE RISK IN BANKING BOOK (IRRBB)

It describes risk reporting and measurement systems: monthly IRS-TGA for Earnings at Risk (EaR) and IRS-DGA for Market Value of Equity (MVE), including EaR's short-term NII impact and MVE's long-term capital impact. It outlines hedging policies using derivatives like Interest Rate Swaps, OIS, Forward Rate Agreements, and Cross Currency Swaps. Quantitative disclosures for State Bank Group include estimated impact on NII (EaR) and MVE under 100 and 200 bps parallel shifts, with specific figures.

structure.title: DF-10: GENERAL DISCLOSURE FOR EXPOSURE RELATED TO COUNTERPARTY CREDIT RISK
structure.summary: The text presents DF-10 general disclosure for counterparty credit risk as of 31.03.2025, comprising qualitative and quantitative sections. Qualitatively, it defines counterparty credit risk and outlines mitigation processes: CRMD sets maximum Permissible Global Exposure Limits for various counterparty types using scoring models; limits are allocated to business units and operating units; and policies/manuals govern counterparty credit risk. Quantitatively, it provides notional and current credit exposure distributions for interest rate swaps, cross currency swaps, currency options, foreign exchange contracts, currency futures, forward rate agreements, others (NDF), and bond FRA, with totals, and states credit derivative transactions are nil.

structure.title: DF-11: COMPOSITION OF CAPITAL

It details Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital instruments and reserves, including common shares, retained earnings, and regulatory adjustments like goodwill, intangibles, and deferred tax assets. It lists Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital instruments, provisions, and related regulatory adjustments. The template includes capital ratios, buffers, national minima, amounts below deduction thresholds, and caps on provisions. Notes explain deferred tax assets, insurance subsidiary investments, and eligible provisions. Numerical data in crores and references to DF-12 are provided. The document also includes footnotes on reserves and covers capital instruments subject to phase-out arrangements.

Step 2 provides a detailed breakdown of reserves and surplus, minority interest, deposits, borrowings, and other liabilities, with reference numbers for regulatory capital components. Step 3 computes Common Equity Tier 1 capital components, including adjustments for goodwill. It notes that DF-13 and DF-14 are available on the bank's website, states DF-15 is not applicable, and includes DF-16 on equity disclosures for banking book positions, covering qualitative policies and quantitative data on investments, fair values, gains/losses, and capital requirements.

structure.title: DF-17: COMPARISON OF ACCOUNTING ASSETS VS. LEVERAGE RATIO EXPOSURE MEASURE

It lists eight line items: total consolidated assets per published financial statements (with values in millions), adjustments for investments in banking/financial/insurance/commercial entities consolidated for accounting but outside regulatory consolidation, adjustments for fiduciary assets excluded from leverage exposure, adjustments for derivative financial instruments, adjustments for securities financing transactions (repos and secured lending), adjustments for off-balance sheet items converted to credit equivalent amounts, other adjustments, and the resulting leverage ratio exposure for the State Bank Group.

structure.title: DF-18: LEVERAGE RATIO COMMON DISCLOSURE TEMPLATE

It also includes DF-GR Additional Disclosures on Group Risk, covering qualitative disclosures for overseas banking and non-banking entities, addressing corporate governance practices, disclosure practices, arm's length policy for intra-group transactions, common marketing and branding, financial support details, adherence to Group Risk Management policy covenants, and a definition of financial support. A list of covered entities is provided.

structure.title: State Bank of India
structure.summary: This notice announces the 70th Annual General Meeting of State Bank of India shareholders, to be held on June 13, 2025, at 2:30 PM via video conferencing/other audio-visual means. The meeting will transact business to discuss and adopt the Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss Account as of March 31, 2025, the Central Board's report on working and activities, and the Auditor's Report. It includes the corporate centre address, Chairman Challa Sreenivasulu Setty's signature, date May 3, 2025, and reference to the Annual Report 2024-25.

structure.title: ANNEXURE
structure.summary: The text provides general instructions for accessing and participating in the Annual General Meeting (AGM) through video conferencing (VC) or other audio-visual means (OAVM) and voting via electronic means, including remote e-voting. It cites MCA Circulars allowing AGMs through VC/OAVM without physical attendance, with the deemed venue being the State Bank Auditorium. Proxy appointment is not available, but body corporates can appoint authorized representatives. Shareholders can join 15 minutes before/after the scheduled time, with participation limited to 1,000 members on a first-come-first-served basis, excluding large shareholders, promoters, institutional investors, directors, key managerial personnel, committee chairpersons, and auditors. Attendance through VC/OAVM counts for quorum. Remote e-voting is provided by NSDL, and the AGM date is June 13, 2025. The Notice is available on the Bank's website, stock exchange websites, and NSDL's website. The AGM complies with the Companies Act, 2013, MCA Circulars, and SEBI Circulars. For joint holders, the first-named person is entitled to vote if votes are not already cast remotely. Members present via VC who did not cast remote votes may vote via e-voting at the AGM for specific resolutions.

nodes.title: Sustainability governance structure

nodes.summary: SBI's sustainability governance structure includes a Board-approved policy, a Corporate Centre Sustainability Committee (CCSC) chaired by the DMD (CCO & CSO) that reviews performance quarterly, and 17 Circle-level Sustainability Committees (CSCs) chaired by CGMs monitoring targets. A centralized ESG & Climate Finance Unit (ESG & CFU) serves as the nodal department for climate finance, handling fund-raising via green instruments and deployment, reporting to the CSO. The vision targets Net Zero by 2055, with 2030 goals of Net Zero Scope 1 & 2 emissions and 7.5-10% green advances. The unit coordinates ESG ratings, green portfolio oversight, regulator engagement, and new green products. Stakeholder engagement and capital types are also mentioned.

nodes.title: Compliance
nodes.summary: The text details the Bank's compliance culture and framework, including governance oversight by the Central Board and Compliance Risk Management Committee, quarterly compliance reviews, and mandatory staff training on KYC/AML/CFT. It outlines implementation of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, compliance awareness meetings across branches, and a network of compliance officials at all levels with checklists and rigorous testing. It also covers AML/CFT monitoring using AMLOCK software with AI/ML risk scoring, suspicious transaction reporting to FIU-IND, ML-TF risk assessments, customer risk categorization, money mule sensitization, and workshops for Regional Rural Banks.

nodes.title: Ethical Conduct
nodes.summary: The text covers the Bank's ethical conduct framework, including its ISO 9001:2015 certified Compliance Function and AML-CFT cell. It highlights the first independent Ethics Department in Indian Public Sector, a Code of Ethics based on STEPS values, and policies like Anti-Bribery, Conflict of Interest, Staff Accountability, Whistle Blower, and Gift Policy. It details the centralized Disciplinary Proceedings Management System (DPMS), the Garima Policy for POSH compliance with a revamped digital portal, and various awareness initiatives like quizzes, webinars, and an Ethical Audit Survey. It also lists numerous policies and frameworks, and describes the Vigilance Department's structure with CVO and Addl. CVOs, along with training for officers and CSPs.

nodes.title: Policies and Framework
nodes.summary: The text covers the Bank's approach to governance, emphasizing ethical conduct and responsible banking. It details initiatives to prevent sexual harassment through the Garima Policy, including webinars, workshops, a revamped digital portal, and a zero-tolerance policy. It describes various ethics awareness programs such as quiz series, broadcast series, and a platform for sharing experiences, along with ethical audit surveys. It mentions workshops, webinars, and online quizzes conducted in FY 2024-25, and the review of accountability and conflict of interest policies. Finally, it lists the Bank's comprehensive policies and frameworks, including the Sustainability and Business Responsibility Policy, Code of Ethics, and others, aligned with NGRBC principles and accessible on the website.

nodes.title: Strengthening Vigilance for Transparency and Integrity

Vigilance Awareness Week 2024 promoted integrity via multiple channels and community outreach. CVC's capacity-building campaign on procurement concluded with a workshop. Training reached over 27,000 officers and 41,000 CSPs, with 1,326 preventive programs and 107 training sessions. AI/ML monitoring identified high-risk branches for proactive investigations. The text also references stakeholder engagement, financial, intellectual, natural, human, and social capital, and various report sections.

Stakeholder engagement and various capitals are mentioned, along with the ISO certification of the Risk Management Department and periodic reviews by internal audit.

nodes.title: Risk Management Framework, Governance, and Three Lines of Defence

It details the three lines of defence model: operational management as primary risk owners, risk/compliance functions providing oversight, and internal audit for independent assurance. Risk frameworks include ERM, policies, risk appetite and culture assessments, and material risk assessment. Market risk management covers policies, focus areas, capital impacts, VaR, stress testing, and model validation. Operational risk management addresses policies, business continuity, resilience, stakeholder confidence, and KRI monitoring. Capital impacts across financial, intellectual, natural, human, and social capitals are noted.

structure.title: Risk Management Governance and Frameworks at the Bank
structure.summary: The page outlines the bank's risk management approach across credit, enterprise/group, and climate change risk. It details policies, focus areas, and impacted capitals for each. Credit risk covers policies like mitigation, model validation, and stress testing, with focus on ESG risks, digitalisation of RAROC, and training. Enterprise and group risk includes ERM, model risk, ICAAP, and group liquidity policies, focusing on risk appetite, culture, and regulatory reporting. Climate change risk management addresses integration into ERM. The ERM process describes a four-step approach (identification, mitigation, assessment, monitoring) and governance through frameworks and committees.

structure.title: Climate Risk Integration and Operational Resilience at SBI
key_items: Factoring in Risk Assessment into ICAAP
Business Continuity and Operational Resilience Policy
Integration of Climate Risks into Risk Management Process
structure.summary: The page covers State Bank of India's annual ICAAP, detailing the identification and analysis of credit, market, operational, liquidity, IRRBB, concentration, and emerging risks, with capital allocation based on assessment. It outlines the Business Continuity and Operational Resilience Policy, including ISO 22301:2012 compliance and regular reviews. It describes integrating climate risks via a Climate Change Risk Management Committee and Policy, classifying physical risks (acute and chronic) and transition risks (policy, legal, technological, market, reputational). The Bank is developing climate risk methodologies and frameworks, measuring financed emissions, and using a Climate Risk Score Card with quantitative and qualitative metrics. It also analyzes physical risk vulnerabilities at domestic branches, offices, and ATMs, and discusses climate-related scenario analysis for portfolio-level risk identification, mitigation, and sustainability integration, following regulatory guidance.

structure.title: Building Risk Culture - Sensitising Employees on Risk Management

A Risk Culture Survey showed strong awareness across staff levels. Special trainings included a "Train the Trainer" webinar on climate risk for faculty to disseminate knowledge, and webinars for credit officials on decarbonisation pathways for sectors to manage climate risk through customer engagement and low-carbon finance. Stakeholder engagement covers Financial, Intellectual, Natural, Human, and Social Capital.

The page also lists capitals: financial, intellectual, natural, human, social.

structure.title: Stakeholder Engagement Overview: Investors, Communities, NGOs, Regulators

Local communities engage monthly through consultations, welfare programmes, CSR activities, and financial literacy, addressing socioeconomic transformation, job creation, and quality of life. structure.title: Information Security

It covers banking and finance terms (e.g., ADB, AML, EBITDA, KYC, NPA-related committees), regulatory and compliance bodies (RBI, SEBI, PFRDA, IFSCA), sustainability and ESG frameworks (BRSR, GRI, SASB, TCFD, UN SDGs, GHG, PCAF), risk management (ERM, IRRBB, RAROC, DRP), technology and security (ATM, BCMS, CISO, SOC, PCI DSS), customer service and inclusion (BC, CSP, SHG, DBT, PMMY), HR and training (HRMS, LMS, STP), and various government schemes and committees, providing a comprehensive reference for all abbreviations used in the report.
